Full output at org/missions/D9/IRPT/IRPT_BCKEND/deliverables/0.9.0_WK_IRPT_BCKEND~4/RT8-AC2_judgment.md. The four answers, each carrying its measurement and no verdict:

1. WHICH HOST RENDERED. IN ROUND 2, NONE -- the render step reads HUMAN-GATED, read from the deployed controller: decision=HUMAN_GATED, host irpt-ycharts-runner (i-0167fd745ad906a66) state=stopped, document_exists=true. THE HOST THE SYSTEM IS BUILT FOR and its limits: t3.medium (2 vCPU / 4 GiB, var.instance_type's own description says 'Chromium needs the headroom'); LIFETIME none of its own -- aws_ec2_instance_state.runner declares 'stopped', so the converged state of that root is a host that exists and is not running, nothing schedules it and it cannot start itself; COST EBS only while stopped plus t3.medium for the minutes it runs, with no idle compute because there is no idle RUNNING state; CONCURRENCY 1 STRUCTURALLY, because ssm:SendCommand is granted against exactly one instance id and one document name; ISOLATION a SECOND document (irpt-export-render-run) so a render and a vendor sign-in are distinguishable in an audit. THE HOST THAT DID RENDER THE FOUR STORED PDFs was round 1's DEVELOPMENT BOX, Playwright driving Chromium via channel='msedge' -- lifetime the battery process, cost zero marginal, concurrency 1, AND NOT AN ESTATE HOST.

2. FONTS -- THE SHARPEST DIVERGENCE, AND IT IS MEASURED. The package DECLARES ['Lato-Regular','Lato-Bold','Lato-Italic'] at manifest.ts (portal HEAD 32a744dcd3). The four stored PDFs, read back from S3 and parsed by render.fonts_embedded(), embed ['AAAAAA+SegoeUI-Bold','BAAAAA+SegoeUI','CAAAAA+TimesNewRomanPSMT'] -- identical across all four. 0 OF 3 DECLARED FONTS ARE EMBEDDED IN 4 OF 4 ARTIFACTS. Nothing failed, because a browser silently substitutes a missing family and emits a valid PDF. Three consequences, ungraded: the package declares fonts it does not ship; fonts_embedded() exists and NOTHING CALLS IT AS A GATE; a substituted font moves line breaks and therefore page count, a field the receipt carries.

3. WHAT CHANGED BETWEEN TWO RENDERS, AND WHY THE CONTENT HASH IS THE IDENTITY. Two fields, both stamped by the print engine and neither derived from the input: /CreationDate (and /ModDate) and the trailer's /ID. Round 1, one frozen bundle rendered twice: 25,231 bytes both times, TWO DIFFERENT raw sha256. Measured again in round 2 with a different instrument -- the three stored v0-11 objects have three different raw sha256 (9aede5a2.../579b85d0.../6954433a...) and ONE normalized content hash (b646b23012...), so the normalizer removes exactly the differing fields and nothing else. THE CONTENT HASH IS THE ARTIFACT'S IDENTITY because 'is this the same document' must not be answered by a digest that changes when nobody changed anything. AND ROUND 2 STOPPED USING EITHER DIGEST AS THE EXPORT'S IDENTITY: export_id = f(bundle_sha256, contract_version), computed before any render; attempt_id explicit; the raw digest stays in the receipt's artifact.sha256 and is not an identity at all. Round 1's defect was using one answer for two different questions (row IRPT_BCKEND-W4-S12).

4. WHAT THE EXCLUSION PROOF DOES NOT COVER. (i) A READER ADDED LATER IS NOT COVERED -- the four readers are a list this cell wrote by recall, and nothing (no type, no decorator, no gate) forces a fifth to call exclusion.is_excluded. (ii) A READER OUTSIDE THIS REPOSITORY IS NOT COVERED AT ALL: the portal's own fetch, an Athena or Glue read, an S3 Inventory report, a lifecycle rule and a human at the console all address these keys and none imports a Python module. (iii) THE KEY PREDICATE IS AN ENUMERATION AND ENUMERATIONS LAPSE SILENTLY -- this cell's own generation was missing from it for one run, so the proof's blind spot was demonstrated BY the proof (row W4-S18). (iv) THE POPULATION WAS CHOSEN BY THE PROVER: the census reads two prefixes this cell named, and a narrow denominator is how an exclusion proof passes over what it missed. (v) EXCLUSION IS NOT ABSENCE -- the objects still head 200; deletion is Andrew's word and is carried here unexercised.

ONE FINDING THE CRITERION DID NOT ASK FOR, SURFACED BY ANSWERING IT, AND FILED AS ROW IRPT_BCKEND-W4-S19: the three v0-11 exports were built from THREE DIFFERENT bundles (round-1 battery: 38753e307c2e, 86c38f465c00, 9f89d01d4fa7) and their PDFs are CONTENT-IDENTICAL -- one content hash, and an identical decompressed content-stream length of 71,944 bytes. A renderer whose output does not vary with its input cannot be evidence that the input was rendered, and round 1's arm could not see it because every check it ran was per-object. This bears on the grade of IB-s-14, not of IB-rt-8.

mutant.description: FIVE difference controls, each required to produce the NEGATIVE result so the passing arm beside it means something. (1) AN UNSUPPORTED RenderPackage VERSION, which must be REFUSED by code rather than skipped -- otherwise arm (b)'s version gate is a description. (2) A CHANGED BUNDLE in arm (d): the identity must DIFFER, or 'stable across a retry' is indistinguishable from 'constant'. (3) THE REVOKED GRANT in arm (a): the artifact record stays in place and the cache is NOT cleared, so only the grant moves and the refusal cannot be a missing-object error.
